screens.prompt: In B7, return the most recent price logged for the SKU in A7, which the log records twice.

hints.syntax: Start with = and close every bracket: =XLOOKUP(A7,A2:A6,B2:B6,,0,-1).
hints.func-xlookup: XLOOKUP takes six arguments here: the key, the keys, the prices, the text to show when nothing matches, the match mode, and the search direction.
hints.require-ref: Point the first argument at the cell holding the SKU. Typing the SKU into the formula answers for one row and freezes the moment the cell changes.
hints.value: That is the first entry for the SKU, not the latest one. Search mode 1 walks the keys from the top down, and the log appends, so the newest entry is the last match.
hints.error: Read the code: #N/A means the key was not found in the range you searched, and #VALUE! means the key range and the price range are different sizes, so there is no row to pair with.

screens.prompt: The bar's third argument points at an empty column, so give it the range that holds the price.
screens.alt: The lesson's sheet: SKU in column A and price in column B for rows 2 to 6, and row 7 asking for TX-101. The formula bar reads =XLOOKUP(A7,A2:A6,C2:C6,,0,-1) with C2:C6 underlined in red as the third argument, and column C is empty.

hints.value: The third argument is the range XLOOKUP reads the answer from, so it covers the price column's data rows. Rows 2 to 6 hold the log; row 7 is where the answer goes.

docs.explain: The log is append-only, so the newest price for a SKU is the last row that names it. Search mode -1 walks the key column from the bottom up until the first match. TX-101 appears in rows 2 and 4, and the answer is row 4's 21.5. With the default search mode the same formula answers 19.99, a real price from a real row, wrong only because it is the wrong day's price. The fourth and fifth arguments are skipped with empty commas, because there is no missing-value text and the match stays exact. So the search direction is the sixth argument and cannot be moved. A sorted log with VLOOKUP approximate match, or a MAXIFS over the date column, reaches the same number, but both depend on an order the sheet has to keep. This one reads the order the sheet already has.

errors.text: The key is not in the range XLOOKUP searched, which happens when the key range points at the price column or stops before the last row.
The key range and the return range are different sizes, so a row in one has nothing to pair with in the other.

docs.atWork: Price logs, stock movements and status changes where the same key is written again on a later date, so the newest row wins.
docs.outcome: Return the newest entry for a key in an append-only log without sorting or filtering it first.

seo.title: XLOOKUP search mode in Excel: newest row
seo.description: Search mode -1 walks an append-only log from the bottom, so a repeated SKU returns its latest price: 21.5 instead of the 19.99 logged first.
